'''''Holocarpha heermannii''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Asteraceae]] known by the common name '''Heermann's tarweed'''.  It is [[Endemism|endemic]] to [[California]].

==Distribution==
''Holocarpha heermannii'' grows in the hills, mountains, and valleys of the central and southern part of California. It is most common in the [[Inner Coast Ranges]] in the eastern [[San Francisco Bay Area]], the southern [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierra Nevada]] foothills, and the [[Tehachapi Mountains]]. It is also found in the Southern Outer [[California Coast Ranges]] and western [[Transverse Ranges]].<ref>[http://www.calflora.org/entry/dgrid.html?crn=4204 CalFlora taxon report, University of California, ''Holocarpha heermannii''  (E. Greene) Keck, Heermann's tarweed ] . accessed 11.14.2013</ref><ref name=tabby>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250066962 Flora of North America, ''Holocarpha heermannii'' (Greene) D. D. Keck, 1958.]</ref>

==Description==
''Holocarpha heermannii'' is an annual herb growing mostly erect from {{convert|20|cm|in}} to over {{convert|1|m|ft}} in height. The stem is densely glandular and coated in short and long hairs. The leaves are up to {{convert|10|cm|in}} long near the base of the plant and those along the stem are smaller.<ref name=tabby/>

The [[inflorescence]] is a spreading array of branches bearing clusters of [[head (botany)|flower heads]]. Each flower head is lined with [[bract|phyllaries]] which are coated in large bulbous resin glands. They are hairy and sticky in texture. The head contains many yellow disc florets surrounded by three to 10 golden yellow ray florets.<ref name=tabby/>

The ray and fertile disc florets produce [[achene]]s of different shapes.<ref name=tabby/>
